title: Amazon EC2 m7i.metal-24xl instance is now generally available for VMware Cloud on AWS
summary: AWS announces the general availability of Amazon EC2 m7i.metal-24xl instance for VMware Cloud on AWS. This offering features a disaggregated storage architecture from compute, supporting both Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and VMware Cloud Flex Storage as primary storage options for customers. ...
text:
AWS announces the general availability of Amazon EC2 m7i.metal-24xl instance for VMware Cloud on AWS. This offering features a disaggregated storage architecture from compute, supporting both Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and VMware Cloud Flex Storage as primary storage options for customers. With this new offering, customers can now choose among three instance types for VMware Cloud on AWS: i3en.metal, i4i.metal and m7i.metal-24xl.
This diskless instance allows customers to choose their storage and compute options independently, providing flexibility, control, and optimized infrastructure.
Powered by custom 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, the m7i.metal-24xl instance is ideal for customers with compute-intensive workloads. It also offers accelerated performance with the Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel® AMX) accelerator, well-suited for deep learning (DL) inference and training workloads. With up to 48 physical cores, 348GiB of memory, the m7i instances when used with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP will offer a great solution for use cases such as disaster recovery, backup infrastructure, compute intensive, and AI / ML applications.
VMware Cloud on AWS customers can leverage the m7i.metal-24xl instance in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland) Europe (Stockholm).
Customers now have 3 instance type options for new deployments: m7i.metal-24xl, i4i.metal, and i3en.metal. To learn more about the capabilities and benefits of m7i.metal-24xl instance, connect with your AWS representative or contact us here.

title: VMware Cloud on AWS is now available in Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) region
summary: Today, we are excited to announce the availability of VMware Cloud on AWS in Asia Pacific (Hyderabad). The addition of this region expands the availability of VMware Cloud on AWS to 26 regions globally, enabling more customers to accelerate their migration to the cloud. ...
text:
Today, we are excited to announce the availability of VMware Cloud on AWS in Asia Pacific (Hyderabad). The addition of this region expands the availability of VMware Cloud on AWS to 26 regions globally, enabling more customers to accelerate their migration to the cloud.
VMware Cloud on AWS is a jointly engineered solution that seamlessly integrates computing, networking, and storage functionalities, while benefiting from the dedicated maintenance, support, and operations from both VMware and AWS. Customers can leverage the same familiar VMware tools, skill sets, and governance across their on-premises and cloud environments, while taking advantage of the scalability and cost-effectiveness of the AWS cloud. AWS is VMware’s preferred public cloud partner for all vSphere-based workloads. Customers can also deploy the entire VMware stack, including ESXi, vCenter, NSX and vSAN, along with additional storage options while getting access to over 200 native AWS services. This new availability in Hyderabad allows customers to leverage the scale and sustainability of all AWS data centers.
The new offering is available for purchase through both AWS and VMware, as well as through the companies' respective partners. To learn more about VMware Cloud on AWS, visit our page or connect with your AWS sales representative.

title: AWS Backup now supports restore of VMware workloads to Amazon EC2
summary: AWS Backup now supports restoring VMware backups to Amazon EC2. This allows you to restore your VMware backups directly in EC2, as EC2 native instances. AWS Backup can restore to on-premises VMware, VMware CloudTM on AWS Outposts, VMware CloudTM on AWS, and Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). AWS Backup also supports restoring virtual machines (VMs) at the VM-level or disk-level. ...
text:
AWS Backup now supports restoring VMware backups to Amazon EC2. This allows you to restore your VMware backups directly in EC2, as EC2 native instances. AWS Backup can restore to on-premises VMware, VMware CloudTM on AWS Outposts, VMware CloudTM on AWS, and Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). AWS Backup also supports restoring virtual machines (VMs) at the VM-level or disk-level.
AWS Backup support for restore of VMware workloads to Amazon EC2 provides you a simple and cost-effective method of migrating your on-premises VMware workloads to AWS and meet your data recovery requirements across VMware environments. AWS Backup provides a consistent data protection experience from on premises to Cloud, helping you meet your business and regulatory compliance needs. You can use a single policy in AWS Backup to simplify data protection and automate lifecycle management of your VMware environments alongside the supported AWS storage, compute, and database services.
AWS Backup for VMware is available in the US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (N. California, Oregon), AWS GovCloud (US-East, US-West), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Paris, Stockholm), South America (Sao Paulo), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong, Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Osaka), Middle East (Bahrain), and Africa (Cape Town) Regions. To learn more about AWS Backup for VMware, visit the product page and documentation. To get started, visit the AWS Backup console.

title: Announcing General Availability of Amazon EC2 i4i.metal instance for VMware Cloud on AWS
summary: We are excited to announce the general availability of i4i.metal instance for VMware Cloud on AWS. Designed for storage I/O intensive workloads, i4i.metal instance is powered by 3rd generation Intel® Xeon® Ice Lake processor with an all-core turbo frequency of 3.5 GHz, offer up to 30% better compute price performance over i3 instances. ...
text:
We are excited to announce the general availability of i4i.metal instance for VMware Cloud on AWS. Designed for storage I/O intensive workloads, i4i.metal instance is powered by 3rd generation Intel® Xeon® Ice Lake processor with an all-core turbo frequency of 3.5 GHz, offer up to 30% better compute price performance over i3 instances. This new instance is intended for VMware Cloud on AWS customers looking for an optimal balance of compute, memory, and storage configuration.
Compared to the i3 instances, i4i.metal offers twice the storage at 30TiB of raw local NVMe flash storage, around 1.8 times more processing power at 128 vCPUs, processor running 1.5 times faster at 3.5GHz Turbo, twice the memory at 1,024 GiB and networking speed up to 75Gbps, 3x faster than i3.metal. The i4i.metal instance is a highly secure instance type with support for host-to-host encryption enabled by default. The high memory, CPU, and storage configuration of the i4i.metal instances is ideal for workloads that need fast access to datasets on local storage.
The i4i.metal instance type is now available to purchase in US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), US West (N. California), Canada (Central), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Paris), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). It will be available in additional regions over the coming months.
Customers can choose to deploy a new SDDC with the i4i.metal instance or migrate their workloads from existing i3.metal and/or i3en.metal nodes to the new i4i.metal instance. To learn more about the capabilities and benefits of the i4i.metal instance connect with the VMware Cloud on AWS team.

title: Announcing VMware Cloud on AWS integration with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
summary: AWS and VMware now offer a supplemental, jointly-engineered network file system (NFS) datastore option for VMware Cloud on AWS so you can reduce costs and accelerate your migration to the cloud. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a fully managed service that allows you to run NetApp ONTAP file systems on AWS. ...
text:
AWS and VMware now offer a supplemental, jointly-engineered network file system (NFS) datastore option for VMware Cloud on AWS so you can reduce costs and accelerate your migration to the cloud. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a fully managed service that allows you to run NetApp ONTAP file systems on AWS. With this integration, you can attach scalable, high-performance storage, independent from your compute resources, to your VMware Cloud on the AWS Software Defined Data Center (SDDC).
To get started, visit the VMware Cloud on AWS website. For more information, visit the FSx for NetApp ONTAP documentation or the AWS News blog.
